q8.answer: The merge first keeps only the newest staged row per order_id (ROW_NUMBER by updated_at DESC, own run_id only). Then MERGE updates a matched core.orders row only when s.updated_at > t.updated_at, so equal or older versions are skipped and re-runs are harmless.

q9.answer: It is stored in the warehouse table ops.etl_state (one row per pipeline, high_water_mark timestamptz). It is set to GREATEST(HWM, hi), where hi is the replica's now() taken when the snapshot opened. This happens in step 6, in the same warehouse transaction as the merge and the run_log committed update.

q10.answer: The merge into core.orders, the HWM advance and the run_log update all happen in one warehouse transaction, so dashboards see either the previous night or the full new night. The dashboards read only core.orders, never staging. If the warehouse lacks snapshot isolation for readers, the fallback is to merge into a shadow table and swap it atomically.

q11.answer: A failed attempt's core.orders and HWM are unchanged. Its staged rows carry its old run_id, so the retry ignores them. The retry deletes staging rows of runs that are no longer running and extracts with its own run_id. The retry reads the unchanged HWM, so it recomputes lo = HWM - 2h and a fresh hi, covering the same ground plus anything newer.

q12.answer: It re-reads all rows of each mismatched order-creation day from the replica, in one REPEATABLE READ snapshot, into stg.orders_recon. It checks the staged count against a count(*) over the same days. It applies them in one warehouse transaction using the same guarded merge (newer updated_at only), after checking its own run_log row is still running. It does not touch the nightly high-water mark.
